_source: Ministry of Education / Curriculum Development Centre, Zambia. 'English Syllabus, Grade 10-12' (2013, published by CDC) — Grade 11, Topics 11.1-11.5. Topic, sub-topic and Specific Outcome statements only; the 'Content' column is omitted for the reasons documented in the Grade 10 file. Two sub-topics under 11.3 (Composition) — 'Writing Minutes' and 'Writing Speeches' — have no directly visible numbered outcome sentence in the source extraction (the printed table cell appears to have lost the outcome text while keeping its Skills/Values columns); their outcomes were reconstructed from the clearly attributable skill statements ('Application of knowledge on writing minutes' and 'Application of knowledge on making a vote of thanks'), matching the equivalent Grade 10 sub-topics. Under 11.5.1 (Relative Clauses), the source prints the exact same outcome sentence and example twice (as outcomes 1 and 6); the duplicate is not reproduced. The syllabus organizes content by Grade only, not by Term, so all of Grade 11 is modeled as a single term here.

competencies.description: Impart and seek factual information in giving verbal reports and oral messages
Express and find out intellectual attitudes when making inquiries
Express and find out emotional attitudes when addressing people of different classes, age groups and sexes
Interpret, express and find out moral attitudes when expressing beliefs and strongly held opinions without giving offence
Get things done
Use socially appropriate language in different situations
Read passages with understanding and recall the details
Locate details and answer factual questions
Show understanding of the underlying meaning of texts
Describe the feelings, qualities and motives of characters in stories
Read appropriate unabridged books
Read a wide variety of texts: newspapers, magazines, journals etc
Read critically and make discriminating judgements
Practise reading for purpose (e.g. newscast)
Write advanced descriptive compositions
Write advanced narrative compositions
Write advanced essays in other subjects
Write essays on given topics from other subjects
Write newspaper and magazine articles
Write book reports
Write minutes of a meeting
Write a vote of thanks
Report a message summarizing main points
Give a speech summarizing main points (e.g. making announcements)
Tabulate specific information in the text or other print materials such as maps, graphs, tables and charts
Summarise given texts
Use 'which' or 'that' with subjects that are people
Use 'which' or 'that' with subjects that are things
Use 'whom', 'who' or nothing with objects that are things
Use preposition + relative pronoun with objects that are people
Use 'which', 'that' or nothing with objects that are things
Use likely/probable conditional sentences
Use unlikely/improbable conditional sentences
Use impossible conditional sentences
Use common variations of conditional sentences
Use 'unless' in conditional sentences
Use 'even if' to indicate condition and implied contrast
Use direct speech
Change direct speech into reported speech
